requirement: Download an HTTP response to a file with aiohttp without buffering it in memory, refusing bodies larger than a byte limit either from the announced Content-Length or while streaming, and never leaving a partial file behind.
skeleton: A TooLargeError carrying the limit and download checking status and Content-Length, streaming iter_chunked into the destination with a running total, and removing the file when the cap is exceeded.
caption: Streaming a download to disk with aiohttp under a hard size cap. TooLargeError(limit) stores the limit and reads response exceeds limit bytes. download(session, url, dest, *, max_bytes) opens session.get inside async with and calls resp.raise_for_status first, so a 404 raises aiohttp.ClientResponseError before any file is created. A Content-Length larger than max_bytes raises TooLargeError before the body is read. Otherwise the body is written in CHUNK_BYTES pieces from resp.content.iter_chunked into dest opened with wb, replacing old contents, and a running total above max_bytes raises TooLargeError; a body of exactly max_bytes is allowed. On TooLargeError the partial file is unlinked and the error re-raised. It returns the byte count. The fixture asserts, with an aiohttp TestServer, that 2000 bytes at a 2000 cap are written and returned, that an existing file is overwritten, that a chunked 3000-byte stream at 2500 raises TooLargeError with limit 2500 and leaves no file, that an announced 5000-byte length at 1000 raises TooLargeError, and that a 404 raises ClientResponseError with no file.

plan.intent: Fetch user-supplied URLs to disk without letting a huge body fill memory or disk
constraints: Error statuses raise aiohttp.ClientResponseError via raise_for_status before writing
A Content-Length above max_bytes raises TooLargeError before reading
The body streams through iter_chunked and a total above max_bytes raises TooLargeError
The destination is overwritten, and removed when TooLargeError is raised

rationale.teaches: Stream with resp.content.iter_chunked, enforce a cap both from Content-Length and from the running total, and clean up partial output on failure.
rationale.why: resp.read() on untrusted URLs buffers unbounded bodies, trusting only Content-Length misses chunked responses, and leftover partial files look like valid downloads.

ops.docstring: Stream an aiohttp download to disk under a hard size cap.

ops.source:
async def download(
    session: aiohttp.ClientSession, url: str, dest: Path, *, max_bytes: int
) -> int:
    """Stream ``url`` into ``dest`` and return the number of bytes written."""
    async with session.get(url) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        if resp.content_length is not None and resp.content_length > max_bytes:
            raise TooLargeError(max_bytes)
        total = 0
        try:
            with dest.open("wb") as handle:
                async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(CHUNK_BYTES):
                    total += len(chunk)
                    if total > max_bytes:
                        raise TooLargeError(max_bytes)
                    handle.write(chunk)
        except TooLargeError:
            dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise
    return total

candidates.why_wrong: A body of exactly max_bytes is rejected as too large.
An oversized announced Content-Length is not refused up front, so the download starts anyway.
An oversized stream leaves a truncated partial file on disk.
The file is opened for append, so new bytes are glued onto old contents.
Error statuses are not raised, so a 404 page is saved as the download.
